transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’ve been hearing voices that aren't actually there, and it’s been making me feel extremely depressed and exhausted. It has just been really hard to function lately.
Have the voices ever happened during a time when you were not feeling depressed for at least two weeks? Or do they only happen when you’re in a depressive episode?

Yes, I have definitely heard the voices during times when I wasn't feeling depressed. There was a period of about two or three weeks where my mood felt okay, but the voices were still there just as clearly.
Over the whole time you’ve been ill, have you been depressed for most of the time, or have the depression periods been only a smaller part of it?

Yes, I've felt depressed for most of the time. Out of the ten months or so that I've been dealing with all of this, the heavy depression has been there for about five months. It just feels like it's constantly hanging over me.

During those depressed periods, did you also have symptoms like loss of interest, low energy, changes in sleep or appetite, guilt, poor concentration, or thoughts of death nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes, I completely lost interest in everything I used to enjoy and felt constantly drained of energy. I also struggled with sleep, like having trouble falling asleep and waking up too early, and I've had thoughts of wishing I just wouldn't wake up. These feelings have been happening nearly every day for about five months now.
Thinking about the entire 10 months, including when symptoms were milder, would you say the depression was present for more than half of the total time?

Yes, looking back over the entire ten months, I would definitely say the depression has been present for more than half of that time. Even during the milder periods, that heavy, low feeling almost always hung over me. It has really dominated the whole experience.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)", "Schizophrenia"]. Based on this conversation, Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) is now strongly favored because the patient reports: (1) hallucinations persisting for about 2–3 weeks when mood was okay, satisfying the requirement for psychosis outside a mood episode; and (2) a major depressive episode with neurovegetative symptoms and passive death wishes present nearly every day for about five months, with depression present for more than half of the total 10-month illness duration. This pattern makes Schizophrenia less likely because the mood episodes are not a minor part of the illness but instead predominate for the majority of the course. Therefore the current candidate list has narrowed to ["Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)"].

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent auditory hallucinations, including a 2–3 week period when mood was not depressed but voices continued, establishing psychosis outside a mood episode. Depressive symptoms meeting a major depressive episode have been present nearly daily for about five months and for more than half of the total 10-month illness duration, supporting schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.
